input.quote: This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
input.rationale: Section 13 provides automatic successive one-year renewals terminable on 30 days' written notice by either party, which satisfies the fallback (and indeed the preferred) notice-window and renewal-term parameters. However, renewal pricing is unconstrained: Section 6 freezes Hosting Services costs only "for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement", so TrueLink may reprice at each renewal without limit. That fails the fallback requirement that renewal price increases be capped at 5%. Our proposal is the shortest fallback-level cure: a 5% ceiling on fee increases in any renewal term, leaving the existing renewal and notice mechanics untouched. We are not pressing the preferred CPI/3% cap or the 60-day Vendor reminder.

mappings.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
mappings.quote: unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year

mappings.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The 30-day non-renewal notice and successive one-year renewal terms are acceptable to us, but fees are only frozen for the first year, so renewals could reprice without limit. We have added our fallback cap of 5% on any fee increase in a renewal term.

ops.text: TrueLink's fees will not increase by more than five percent (5%) in any renewal term.
